tools.name: get_market_status
tools.description: Returns Ed25519-signed market-state receipt for pre-trade verification and pre-execution gating across 28 global exchanges. Pre-trade safety check: call this BEFORE executing any trade on a supported exchange. Model-agnostic: works identically regardless of which AI model consumes it — GPT-5 nano, C

tools.name: get_market_schedule
tools.description: Returns holiday-aware trading session schedule with next open/close UTC timestamps for any of 28 exchanges. Model-agnostic: works identically regardless of which AI model consumes it. Pairs with get_market_status signed receipts. WHEN TO USE: planning trade execution windows; checking market hours,

tools.name: list_exchanges
tools.description: Returns directory of all 28 exchanges supported by Headless Oracle: MIC codes, exchange names, IANA timezones, market hours metadata, and mic_type (iso|convention). Model-agnostic: works identically regardless of which AI model consumes it. WHEN TO USE: call once at agent startup to discover support

tools.name: get_payment_options
tools.description: Returns available payment and authentication options for accessing live market data. Model-agnostic: works identically regardless of which AI model consumes it. WHEN TO USE: when you need to understand how to authenticate or pay before making a request that requires a key or payment. Returns upgrade

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_exchanges" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Returns directory of all 28 exchanges supported by Headless Oracle: MIC codes, exchange names, IANA timezones, market hours metadata, and mic_type (iso|conventi…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_market_status" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
